terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

objectClass.notes: Subtype confirmed Classic Knife from hammer-head crossguard, 5-step staircase butt, diamond-quilted slab grip, gold beaded ferrule, 6-notch spine jimping and deep semicircular choil. Not a Bayonet/M9 (no fuller, no straight bar guard), not a Bowie (no clip point), not a folder.

reasoning: Silhouette carries three separate cut systems: 6-notch spine jimping, a 5-step staircase butt and a deep semicircular choil between guard spur and blade heel.
Repetition systems: jimping array (6), butt steps (5), diamond-quilt grid (~12x5), bolster screws (2 per bolster x 2 bolsters x 2 faces).
The Fade finish is the item: its gradient placement and wavy lower-zone boundary are identity-defining and must come from projected reference pixels, not a generic ramp.
Eight distinct material zones share one silhouette, so material segmentation along X drives the build as much as geometry does.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Choose simple/moderate/complex/ultra-complex from observed structure, not from a hardcoded domain.

details.observation: 6 rounded U jimping scallops, pitch 29px, depth ~10px, spanning px x 879-1041 (centres 887/916/945/974/1003/1032)
deep semicircular choil: bottom edge rises to y=620px between the guard spur (y=712) and the blade heel (y=706), arc spans px x 725-878
drop-point: spine flat at y=442px to x=1425 then curves down to the tip at (1995,538); edge sweeps up from y=664 at x=1560

primary flat grind: a straight tonal break running from the ricasso up toward the tip, splitting the face into an upper flat and a lower bevel; a second short facet line sits above it near the ricasso
Fade lower zone: darker desaturated blobs with rounded wavy tongue-shaped tops along the bottom third of the blade -- the Fade's characteristic flame-lick edge
Fade order tip->ricasso: violet #4a3a6a / blue #3f3f68 at the tip, magenta-crimson #7a1529 mid-forward, amber #744c25 mid-rear, bare warm steel #86776f at the ricasso
a narrow bright secondary edge bevel runs the whole cutting edge, lighter and less saturated than the face above it
hammer-head crossguard: forward-canted upright quillon peaking at (750,380)px, wide trapezoid body, rounded downward spur reaching (682,712)px
a dark vertical band down the guard's blade-side edge is the guard's own Z side face -- the guard is visibly thicker than the blade it brackets
details.note: thickness ratio inferred from the width of the visible side face

details.observation: gold/brass beaded-braided collar band, px x 566-643, bright specular beads over a dark ground -- the only warm-metal part on the knife
two countersunk socket screws in the fore-bolster plate, upper at ~(530,510)px, lower at ~(530,585)px, each with a chamfered recess ring
large diamond-quilted relief across px x 160-484: ~12 columns x ~5 rows of raised soft-edged diamonds, pitch ~30x28px, distinctly puffy rather than sharp knurl
two more countersunk screws in the rear bolster, upper ~(108,550)px, lower ~(122,614)px -- 4 screws per face in total
5-step staircase cut in the butt plate's top edge: plateaus at y=592/572/552/532/512px, each ~18-20px wide and 20px tall, climbing toward the grip
lanyard hole centred ~(56,618)px, radius ~24px, with a countersunk chamfer ring and a bright bare-steel bore visible through it
a thin bright polished strip separates the butt plate from the rear bolster (px x ~78-84), reading as an exposed liner/spacer edge
the grip is a wedge: silhouette height falls from 170px at the butt to 130px at the ferrule, the bottom edge rising more steeply than the top
the Fade does not reach the ricasso: px x 785-900 stays bare warm satin steel, brighter on the back view than the front
edges and high points show only light lightening; no paint loss to bare metal on the blade face -- consistent with a low-wear finish
details.note: 'Minimal Wear' is a user-supplied label; float value is not measurable from pixels

details.observation: the anodized face carries a broad soft anisotropic sheen along the blade's long axis rather than a tight point highlight

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

Hammer-head guard: canted quillon + lower spur

Gold ferrule + four bolster screws per face
Diamond-quilt relief reads as soft raised diamonds

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: single-image extraction is reference-derived inference, not exact photogrammetry

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold
reference lighting copied without separating material readability

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions.thickness: INFERRED (confidence 0.45) - both supplied views are broadside

assumptions.hiddenRegions: extrusion walls and the bore interior are authored, not observed

normal map response visible on quilt, beads and screw recesses

buildPasses.intent: Project the de-lit reference crop per face as albedo ONLY, then drive response from independent channels: a per-zone roughness map (blade 0.17 to grip 0.72, with a polished 0.11 band along the cutting edge), a per-zone metalness map, an authored normal map carrying the quilt grid, ferrule beads, screw dimples and lanyard chamfer, and a cavity AO map. Roughness variation and normal response are both required; displacement is not used.

buildPasses.goal: Add procedural surface locality such as normal/bump/displacement, AO, dirt, stains, chips, grain, moss, scratches, and wear.
acceptance: Every required material feature group has local overrides or surfaceDetail tied to evidenceRefs.
A grazing-angle close-up proves that normal/height detail breaks highlights naturally and does not read as smooth plastic.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make material and form readable under neutral turntable lighting plus optional reference lighting.
acceptance: lightingFromPhoto identifies key light direction/color/intensity, fill light, rim or environment light, and ambient color.
Exposure, tone mapping, background color/gradient, shadow softness, and contact shadow behavior are specified.
Lighting does not hide geometry/material gaps and screenshots can be compared fairly to the reference.
Neutral, grazing, and reference-matched lighting checks distinguish material errors from lighting errors.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make the model ready for future animation, transformation, physics, or destruction.

buildPasses.goal: Protect runtime performance after visual fidelity is accepted.
acceptance: Triangle count, draw calls, instancing, LOD strategy, and FPS target are documented or verified.

reviewHistory.summary: Reference-projection Classic Knife: traced silhouette IoU 0.9848, Divine Eye fidelity 0.9068 (target 0.85), every material zone within +/-8/255 of the FRONT reference, multi-angle non-degenerate. Residual: uniform lightness deficit ~5/255 on blade+guard, stochastic ferrule beads, inferred Z thickness.

Silhouette re-verified after RDP conditioning: IoU 0.9819 front / 0.9831 back, aspect+scale delta 0.0045. Blade columns 648->162 with the jimping span protected from both smoothing and decimation. Map-stripped render confirms the silhouette reads with no materials at all.

Through-tang added spanning x -1.962..-0.452; the six furniture parts are now children of the tang with Y-inset tenons, so attachment.parentSocket='tang' resolves to a real object instead of a dangling name.

Cross-sections roll over a finite-radius edge instead of feathering to zero thickness, rim welded to the face grids: all lofted parts watertight (0 open edges, 0 non-manifold; previously blade 76 open, guard 288 non-manifold). Blade gains a distal taper.

The 9 previously map-only components are real geometry: 8 instanced countersunk screws, a real ExtrudeGeometry lanyard perforation with torus chamfers, instanced ferrule beads and quilt pyramids on the rolled edges where they break the silhouette.
Back-side lamp changed from blue to warm-neutral: back-face hue drift 44.6deg -> -5.1deg, back fidelity 0.8826 -> 0.8945, for 0.001 on the front. blowoutParity 1.0, flatRegionScore 0.9553.
Runtime hierarchy exposes tang/grip/tip/lanyard/guard sockets, per-part attachment records with real overlap, and destruction groups split blade / furniture / core.
Total triangles 82224 -> 29064 (-65%) while ADDING all detail geometry, funded by adaptive blade decimation. Instanced meshes carry the repeated hardware.

Re-review after the metalness solve. The zone maps already hold absolute values (metalness 1.0 on steel, 0.047 on the grip; roughness 0.166 blade / 0.718 grip), so roughness scalars go to 1.0 and metalness is the only tuned scalar: 0.45, solved against the reference's own luma+saturation. Result luma 63.33 vs reference 63.39, orbit luma swing 2.6% -> 9.0%, flatRegionScore 0.8918 -> 0.9553. envMapIntensity deleted after measuring it to be a complete no-op (identical output at 0/3/10 with lamps off); scene.environmentIntensity is the real control.
